stories.title: The Brothers Lumen
stories.logline: Two brothers in a Lyon-like mill town build a box that makes pictures move, then must decide what to film first.
stories.story: Aurèle and Léon Lumen run their father’s glove factory by day and tinker with lenses by night. When their clattering box finally throws a moving image onto a bedsheet, the whole street crowds into the laundry to watch their own neighbours walk across the wall. The brothers argue: film trains, or film people? Their sister settles it by sewing the first costume ever made for a camera.

stories.title: Flicker & Lace
stories.logline: A seamstress becomes cinema’s first costume designer when her hand-tinted gowns make audiences gasp.
stories.story: Odile paints colour frame by frame onto film for a travelling picture show, and her gowns glow scarlet in a black-and-white world. Rival showmen want her brushes, a banker wants her patents, and a shy projectionist wants her attention. Each week a new town, a new tent, and a new dress that has never been seen before because it has never been possible before.

stories.title: The Nickel Palace
stories.logline: A picture house owner bets everything on a single film nobody has finished yet.
stories.story: In 1907, Hattie Marsh buys a derelict opera house and renames it the Nickel Palace. She has sold tickets for a film still being shot on the roof by a director who keeps changing the ending. Opening night arrives with the last reel still drying in the boiler room. The audience waits. The orchestra improvises. The dress on screen is still wet paint.

stories.title: Crank Street
stories.logline: On a street of rival studios, everyone is inventing the movies at once.
stories.story: Six glass-roofed studios share one street and one sun. When clouds come, filming stops and feuds start. There is the stuntman who falls for a living, the actress who writes the title cards, the tailor who dresses every studio and tells none of them the others’ secrets. By the end of the season, Crank Street has invented the close-up, the chase and the star.

stories.title: Silent Seam
stories.logline: A deaf tailor becomes the most sought-after costumier of the silent era, because he already speaks in pictures.
stories.story: Emil has never heard a word the actors say and never needed to. He reads the story in how they move, then cuts clothes that tell it louder. When talking pictures arrive, the studios assume he is finished. He proves the opposite: now that everyone is talking, somebody still has to make the audience feel it.

stories.title: Reel Sisters
stories.logline: Three sisters run the first film studio owned entirely by women.
stories.story: Mabel directs, Josie writes, and little Kit sews and does every stunt the men won’t. Their studio is a converted hat shop with a painted sky on the back wall. Bankers visit and leave confused. Audiences queue round the block. Each episode is a new two-reeler and a new scheme to keep the lights on.

stories.title: The Magic Lantern Ball
stories.logline: At a masked ball in 1899, a projector throws a dress onto a woman who isn’t wearing one, and society loses its mind.
stories.story: An inventor hired to entertain a duchess’s ball projects a gown of light onto a plain-dressed maid. For one dance she is the most beautiful woman in the room. By midnight three counts have proposed and the duchess has fainted. By morning the maid has vanished, and the inventor is searching every kitchen in the city.

stories.title: Talkie Town
stories.logline: When sound arrives in 1929, a studio of silent stars must learn to speak.
stories.story: Voices crack, accents surprise, and a microphone hides in every flower arrangement. The glamorous lead sounds like a goose. The extra with nothing to do sounds like velvet. Costumes rustle too loudly and must be remade in silent silk. Talkie Town is about what happens when a whole industry discovers it has a voice.

stories.title: Skyline 2090
stories.logline: In a city of sky-trams, a tailor dresses the people who live above the clouds and the ones who fix the clouds.
stories.story: Mira’s atelier sits on floor 400, halfway between the penthouses and the weather crews. She makes gowns for the rich and wind-proof suits for the workers, and she knows every secret in between. When the city’s cloud engines start to fail, both sides come to her for something to wear to the end of the world.

stories.title: Chrome Avenue
stories.logline: A robot doorman on the city’s grandest street decides he wants a suit of his own.
stories.story: For forty years Unit 7 has opened doors on Chrome Avenue and admired the tailoring that walks through them. He saves every tip. One spring he walks into the finest atelier in the city and asks to be measured. The tailor has never measured a robot. The robot has never been measured. Both learn something about fit.

stories.title: Monorail Hearts
stories.logline: Commuters on the city’s loop line fall in and out of love between stations.
stories.story: The Loop takes forty minutes and passes twelve stations. Every episode follows a different pair of strangers who share a carriage, a glance, or an umbrella. The conductor sees everything. By the finale we learn the conductor has been riding the loop for one person too.

stories.title: The Glass District
stories.logline: An architect builds a neighbourhood with no walls, then has to live in it.
stories.story: Everything in the Glass District is transparent: homes, shops, even clothes woven from light fibre. Its architect believes privacy is old-fashioned. Then she falls in love, and discovers there are some things she would rather nobody saw. A fable about cities, fashion and the right to close a curtain.

stories.title: Neon Couriers
stories.logline: Bicycle messengers race packages across a vertical city where every floor has a different dress code.
stories.story: Floor 10 is suits. Floor 90 is sequins. Floor 300 is anything that glows. Tam and her crew of couriers change outfits in lifts to make deliveries unnoticed. When one package turns out to hold a stolen design, they have to cross every floor in one night, in every costume they own.

stories.title: The Weather Tailor
stories.logline: In a domed city where the council sets the weather, one tailor learns to sew rain.
stories.story: Nobody in the dome has felt real rain in a century. Ivo, an apprentice tailor, finds an old coat that holds a storm in its lining. When he wears it, it drizzles on him alone. Soon everyone wants a coat with weather in it, and the council wants to know who gave a tailor the sky.

stories.title: Automat
stories.logline: In a city of vending-machine restaurants, the staff who restock them at night run the real city.
stories.story: Behind each little window of pie and coffee is a corridor, and behind the corridors is a night world of cooks, cleaners and couturiers. They trade gossip, favours and hand-me-down finery. When a developer plans to automate them out of existence, the night staff stage a fashion show nobody upstairs will ever forget.

stories.title: Tomorrow’s Parade
stories.logline: On the day the city unveils its future, the float carrying it breaks down.
stories.story: The World of Tomorrow parade has one star attraction: a float showing how everyone will dress in the year 2000. Halfway down the avenue its engine dies. Stuck on the float, three models, a mechanic and a nervous mayor improvise the future live, in front of a million people, with whatever they are wearing.

stories.title: The Wanderer’s Almanac
stories.logline: A fussy tailor takes a job fact-checking the galaxy’s worst-selling travel guide, and every correction he files makes a planet change its mind.
stories.story: Arnold only wanted steady work. Instead he is sent from world to world to check entries like “the locals are friendly” and “formal wear optional”. Each time he corrects one, the planet takes offence and becomes the opposite. By mid-season the galaxy is rearranging itself around his red pen, and the guide is suddenly a bestseller.

stories.title: The Oracle of Hemlines
stories.logline: A moon-sized computer built to decide what everyone should wear answers “whatever you like”, and a civilisation panics.
stories.story: For a thousand years the Velari have dressed exactly as their oracle instructs. When the new model is switched on and politely declines to choose, the capital descends into chaos: nobody has picked an outfit in living memory. A junior technician in mismatched socks becomes, by accident, the most influential person on the planet.

stories.title: The Coincidence Engine
stories.logline: A starship powered by coincidences keeps docking beside the captain’s ex-fiancé.
stories.story: The Serendip runs on unlikely meetings: the more surprising the encounter, the faster it flies. Unfortunately, nothing is more surprising to Captain Juno than bumping into Felix again, on every station, in every sector, always better dressed. Her crew suspects the engine has a sense of humour. Felix suspects something else.

stories.title: The Diner at the Edge of the Map
stories.logline: At the last roadside diner before uncharted space, a waitress draws maps on napkins for travellers who are lost.
stories.story: Past the diner there is nothing on any chart. Pilots stop for pie and directions, and Dot, who has never left, sketches routes from what they tell her. Her napkin maps are passed hand to hand across the frontier. When a traveller brings one back from the far side, marked with her name, she has to decide whether to follow it.

stories.title: Please Mind the Nebula
stories.logline: A tour guide leads bored tourists through the galaxy’s most beautiful sights, which keep trying to eat them.
stories.story: Pip leads coach tours through nebulae, comet tails and a planet made entirely of silk. Her tourists complain about the food, the legroom and the silk planet trying to wrap them up as souvenirs. Each week brings a new sight and a new outfit rule: no sequins near the supernova, no loose scarves in the comet tail.

stories.title: A Brief History of Hats
stories.logline: A historian travels the galaxy to find out why every species independently invented the hat.
stories.story: Dr Oona Velt has a theory: the hat is the one universal. She visits squid poets, crystal bankers and a species that is nothing but a hat. Each one has a reason. None of them agree. The answer, when she finds it, is funnier and sadder than she hoped.

stories.title: Customer Services, Sector Nine
stories.logline: The galaxy’s complaints department handles lost luggage, lost planets and lost tempers.
stories.story: Twelve clerks, one kettle, and every complaint in Sector Nine. Someone’s wedding dress went through a wormhole. Someone’s planet was delivered to the wrong star. The team is overworked, underpaid and extremely well dressed, because the uniform budget was the only thing nobody cut.

stories.title: The Useful Scarf
stories.logline: A weaver on a forgotten moon knits a scarf so handy it accidentally becomes the galaxy’s favourite currency.
stories.story: Hesta’s scarves keep you warm, flag down freighters and double as a picnic blanket. Traders start swapping them instead of coins. Within a year the scarf is legal tender in forty systems and Hesta is being chased by bankers, forgers and a very determined tax inspector. She just wants to finish the next one.

stories.title: One Small Stitch
stories.logline: The seamstresses who hand-sewed the first moonwalk suit, twenty-one layers deep.
stories.story: In a factory better known for bras, a team of women is handed an impossible brief: a suit that keeps a man alive on the Moon. No machine is precise enough; every seam is by hand. As the launch nears, one of them realises the suit will carry her work further than anyone has ever gone. Inspired by the spirit of the space race, told through needles.

stories.title: Mission Control
stories.logline: The people in the room when a rocket leaves, and what they wear to the hardest day of their lives.
stories.story: Short sleeves, thin ties, pocket protectors, and one engineer who insists on a lucky waistcoat. Each episode is a launch day, told from a different desk. By the season finale, somebody is walking on the Moon and everyone in the room is crying into their slide rules.

stories.title: The Astronaut’s Wife
stories.logline: While her husband trains for the Moon, she becomes the most photographed woman in America.
stories.story: Joan never wanted fame. But every magazine wants the astronaut wives on their cover, and every outfit she wears is copied by morning. As launch approaches, she uses her unwanted stage to say what the space program will not: that the family on the ground is on the mission too.

stories.title: Tranquillity Base
stories.logline: The first hotel on the Moon opens with forty guests, one chef and not enough gravity for formal wear.
stories.story: Gowns float, ties drift, and the soufflé never falls. The manager is determined to run it like a grand hotel on Earth. The guests are determined to find out what happens when you dance at one-sixth gravity. Nobody is determined to fix the air conditioning.

stories.title: Earthrise Waltz
stories.logline: A couple on a lunar honeymoon watch the Earth come up and must decide whether to go home.
stories.story: Tess and Marco won the first honeymoon to the Moon in a magazine contest. On the third night, dressed for dinner, they watch the Earth rise over the horizon and realise they have never been this far from their families, or this close to each other.

stories.title: The Space Race Revue
stories.logline: A travelling variety show tours the launch sites, singing about rockets while the real ones keep exploding.
stories.story: Dancers in silver fishnets, a comic in a spacesuit, and a singer who writes a new song for every launch. The Revue follows the rockets from coast to coast, part cheerleader, part conscience. When a launch fails, the show must go on, and the songs start to change.

stories.title: Radio Moon
stories.logline: A teenager with a homemade radio picks up a voice from the Moon that isn’t on any official channel.
stories.story: Danny hears it on a Tuesday: a woman’s voice, calm and faint, describing the view from the lunar surface. No woman has gone to the Moon. He tells his school, his parents, the newspapers. Nobody believes him, except the elderly dressmaker next door, who once sewed a suit that was never used.

stories.title: Rocket Girls
stories.logline: The women who calculated the trajectories, and the dresses they wore to be taken seriously.
stories.story: They were called computers. They did the maths that put people in orbit. Each episode follows one of them through a mission, a battle with a manager, and a wardrobe carefully chosen to be seen but not dismissed. Inspired by the real history of women in early space programs, with invented characters.

stories.title: The Signal from Little Hadley
stories.logline: A radio astronomer in a sleepy English village picks up a message from the stars, and the vicar wants to reply.
stories.story: Dr Margaret Pell’s dish sits behind the cricket pavilion. When it starts receiving a pattern, the whole village has an opinion: the vicar, the postmistress, the retired colonel and the girl who runs the dress shop, who notices the pattern looks exactly like a knitting chart.

stories.title: The Tripod Summer
stories.logline: Three great metal walkers appear in the fields of Kent, and nobody can agree whether to be frightened or offended.
stories.story: They stand very still, very tall, and entirely silent. Farmers complain. The Ministry sends a man in a mac. A young milliner notices the walkers turn to follow anyone wearing a hat with a feather, and realises she may be the only person in England who can talk to them.

stories.title: Professor Quill’s Machine
stories.logline: A tweedy professor builds a time machine in his garden shed and keeps getting the dress code wrong.
stories.story: Every trip he lands in the right place and the wrong clothes: tweed in ancient Rome, a toga in 1970s London. His housekeeper, far more practical, begins packing him period costume. By the finale she is the one operating the machine.

stories.title: The Day the Fog Came Down
stories.logline: A strange fog rolls into London and everyone who walks out of it is wearing different clothes.
stories.story: Bankers emerge in ballgowns, dukes in overalls, a policeman in full Elizabethan ruff. Nobody is harmed. Nobody can explain it. A seamstress from the East End begins mapping the changes and discovers the fog is not random. It is dressing people as who they secretly wish they were.

stories.title: The Ministry of Unlikely Events
stories.logline: A small government department in Whitehall investigates the impossible, on a very small budget.
stories.story: Two civil servants, a filing cabinet and a kettle. This week: a lighthouse that shines backwards, a hedge that grows in tartan, and a village where every wedding dress is identical, no matter who sewed it. Forms must be filled in triplicate. The truth is out there, but it needs a stamp.

stories.title: The Noon Mannequins
stories.logline: Every shop dummy in one market town turns to face the church at exactly noon.
stories.story: Nobody saw them move. The draper swears he locked up. The children think it is marvellous. The adults think it is the Russians. A widowed window-dresser, the only one who talks to mannequins anyway, decides to ask them politely what they want.

stories.title: Mrs Pettigrew’s Wardrobe
stories.logline: In a seaside boarding house, the landlady’s wardrobe opens onto a different decade every morning.
stories.story: Mrs Pettigrew has kept the secret for years: each day the wardrobe in room four leads to another year, and whoever steps through had better be dressed for it. When three new lodgers arrive in the same week, she must teach them the rules, the fashions and the one decade they must never visit.

stories.title: The Last Broadcast
stories.logline: On the final night of a seaside radio station, the presenter starts receiving calls from next week.
stories.story: The station is closing. Reggie, the late-night presenter, plays his last records to an empty town. Then the phones light up with calls from people describing events that have not happened yet, and one caller who asks him, very specifically, not to wear the blue suit tomorrow.

stories.title: Diamonds for Two
stories.logline: Two casino hat-check girls find a diamond in a customer’s hat and spend one wild weekend trying to return it.
stories.story: Lolo is sure it is a sign; Bee is sure it is trouble. The owner never collected his hat, and now a jeweller, a detective and two very charming card sharps all want to know where the stone went. Songs, sequins and a diamond that changes hands nine times before Monday.

stories.title: The Duke and the Chorus Girl
stories.logline: A chorus girl is hired to teach a stiff young duke to tango before a royal wedding.
stories.story: Duke Aurel has two left feet and seven days. Elsie has a matinee every afternoon and a landlady who wants the rent. Their lessons happen in ballrooms, kitchens and one memorable lift. By the wedding he can dance, she can curtsey, and neither of them can stop thinking about the other.

stories.title: The China Doll Revue
stories.logline: A nightclub singer called Mei and her band of misfits run the hottest supper club in a port city full of spies.
stories.story: Every table is a secret and every song is a code. Mei knows everyone’s business and wears a different cheongsam each night, each one hand-embroidered with a message only her friends can read. Comedy, romance and a very dangerous piano.

stories.title: How to Marry a Tailor
stories.logline: Three models open a matchmaking agency that pairs clients by their wardrobes, and get their own matches hopelessly wrong.
stories.story: Tweed goes with tweed, sequins with sequins: that is the theory. Business booms. But when the three founders run their own coats through the system, it matches them with a banker, a burglar and a bus conductor. The agency’s reputation depends on proving the formula works, even when it clearly doesn’t.

stories.title: Sequins & Sass
stories.logline: A troupe of dancers tours the country in a bus held together by hairspray.
stories.story: Nine dancers, one bus, forty costumes and a manager who books them into the wrong town every week. They play weddings, funerals and one very confused military base. Every episode ends with a number, and every number is better than the gig deserves.

stories.title: Swing Shift Couture
stories.logline: A big band stranded in a seaside town takes night jobs in a dress factory to pay the hotel bill, and turns the factory into a hit.
stories.story: The bandleader lost the booking fee on a bet. Now twelve musicians are sewing hems on the night shift, and they cannot help playing while they work. Output doubles, the machinists start dancing, and the factory’s swing-shift dresses become the must-have of the summer. The band has never been so famous for something that isn’t music.

stories.title: The Heiress Hotel
stories.logline: A penniless heiress inherits a grand hotel and must run it without anyone discovering she cannot afford the soap.
stories.story: The guests are royals, film stars and crooks. The staff are loyal, eccentric and unpaid. Dahlia keeps up appearances with borrowed gowns and clever lies, while a handsome auditor checks the books. Screwball chaos in marble corridors.

stories.title: Pearls Before Breakfast
stories.logline: A socialite bets she can live a week as a waitress, and a waiter bets he can live a week as a millionaire.
stories.story: They swap lives on a dare in the same grand hotel. She learns that trays are heavy and tips are politics. He learns that caviar is salty and money is lonely. They keep running into each other in the lift. Neither admits who they really are until the pearls go missing.

stories.title: The Last Fitting
stories.logline: A tailor and a customer meet for one fitting a year, for forty years.
stories.story: Every June, the same client arrives for the same summer suit. Over four decades we watch their lives change between fittings: marriages, losses, wars and wins, all measured in inches taken in and let out. The last fitting is the most tender scene of the season.

stories.title: Paris in the Rain
stories.logline: Two strangers share an umbrella on the Pont des Arts and agree to meet there again in one year.
stories.story: She is a milliner; he is a photographer passing through. They talk for one hour and part without names. A year later she returns, with a hat she has made just for the meeting, and waits. What happens next depends on the weather, the trains and a very persistent pigeon.

stories.title: Letters in the Lining
stories.logline: A seamstress finds love letters sewn into the lining of vintage coats, and sets out to deliver them.
stories.story: Each coat that comes into Rosa’s shop hides a letter never sent. She starts delivering them, decades late. Some recipients are gone. Some are waiting. One is the man in the flat upstairs, who has been writing letters of his own.

stories.title: The Wedding Dress Thief
stories.logline: A bride-to-be discovers her dress has been stolen, and the thief sends her a note apologising.
stories.story: Days before her wedding, Clara’s gown vanishes. A note arrives: it was for a good cause, and she will get it back. Clara follows a trail of clues across the city with the charming detective her fiancé hired, and starts to wonder if she was marrying the right man at all.

stories.title: Summer at the Atelier
stories.logline: A student spends a summer apprenticed to a famous designer on the coast, and falls for everything.
stories.story: The sea, the fabric, the designer’s son and the designer’s rival. Nell arrives knowing nothing and leaves knowing everything, including that some seams are meant to be unpicked. A warm, sunlit romance with a new dress in every episode.

stories.title: Starlight Waltz
stories.logline: An aging film star and a young costume designer find each other on the last night of a great studio.
stories.story: The lot is being sold. Everyone is packing up. The star wanders into wardrobe to return her most famous gown and finds the designer who has been keeping it pressed for thirty years. They dance among the rails until dawn.

stories.title: Two Tickets to the Moon
stories.logline: A pair of rivals win a contest to fly to the first lunar resort together, and must pretend to be engaged.
stories.story: Amelia and Jack cannot stand each other. The contest requires a couple. Now they are on a rocket, sharing a cabin, a wardrobe and a very convincing lie. The Moon, it turns out, is extremely romantic.

stories.title: The Button Box
stories.logline: An old woman leaves her grandson a box of buttons; each one tells the story of a love.
stories.story: Sorting through the tin after the funeral, Sam finds a label on every button: a date, a name, a place. He tracks them down one by one and pieces together a grandmother he never knew: dancer, spy, runaway, and a woman who loved fiercely and often.

stories.title: House of Marchetti
stories.logline: Three generations of a fashion family fight over the business, the name and the last great pool.
stories.story: When the founder dies, her children and grandchildren descend on the atelier in Milan. The will is unclear, the books are worse, and the final pool is unfinished. Each episode reveals a new secret stitched into the family’s history.

stories.title: The Mill
stories.logline: In a northern mill town, a weaver’s daughter fights to keep the looms turning after the owner walks away.
stories.story: The mill has clothed the town for a century. When the owner shuts it, Annie organises the workers to run it themselves. They weave cloth nobody has ordered and sell it to people who cannot afford it, until a designer from London sees the fabric and changes everything.

stories.title: Backstage
stories.logline: The hours before a fashion show, told from every corner of the tent.
stories.story: Models, dressers, the florist, the security guard and the designer throwing up in a bucket. Each episode is the same two hours from a different point of view. By the last episode we understand how the show nearly didn’t happen, and why it did.

stories.title: The Draper’s Daughter
stories.logline: In 1920s Harlem, a young woman turns her father’s fabric shop into the heart of a renaissance.
stories.story: Musicians, poets and dancers all need clothes, and Vera knows exactly what each of them should wear. Her shop becomes the place where the era is dressed. When the crash comes, she must decide what to sell and what to save.

stories.title: The Understudy
stories.logline: An understudy finally gets her chance on the night the star goes missing.
stories.story: Grace has learned every line, every step and every costume change for three years. Tonight the star has vanished and the curtain rises in an hour. Across the season we learn where the star went, why, and what Grace had to do with it.

stories.title: Widow’s Black
stories.logline: A widow opens a mourning-dress shop and becomes the most sought-after confidante in the city.
stories.story: Everyone who comes to Adelaide is grieving. She fits them in black and listens. Over one winter she hears confessions, alibis and a secret that could bring down a family, and must decide whether a dressmaker’s silence is worth more than the truth.

stories.title: The Stylist
stories.logline: A celebrity stylist knows every star’s secrets, and one of them wants her silenced.
stories.story: Nina dresses the most famous people on the planet. She knows who wears padding, who has debts, who is in love with whom. When a star dies in one of her gowns, she becomes the prime suspect and the only person who can find out what really happened.

stories.title: What the Dress Remembers
stories.logline: A wedding dress passed down through five generations narrates the lives of the women who wore it.
stories.story: It was made in 1901, altered in 1928, dyed in 1946, cut short in 1968 and restored in 2026. The dress tells us what it saw: joy, fear, a war, a scandal and a great-granddaughter who almost did not wear it at all.

stories.title: The Veiled Salon
stories.logline: A seamstress discovers the mirrors in Salon Javis show the season to come.
stories.story: A seamstress discovers the mirrors in Salon Javis show the season to come.

stories.title: Shade & Silk
stories.logline: Four models, one gown, and a rivalry that lasts a whole season.
stories.story: Four models, one gown, and a rivalry that lasts a whole season.

stories.logline: A tailor’s apprentice must finish a dinner suit before the estate’s last ball.
stories.story: A tailor’s apprentice must finish a dinner suit before the estate’s last ball.

stories.title: Tails at Midnight
stories.logline: A ballroom farce of swapped coats and borrowed titles.
stories.story: A ballroom farce of swapped coats and borrowed titles.

stories.title: A Bridge in Reye
stories.logline: A shop girl and a runaway prince spend one day on the bridge of Via Reye.
stories.story: A shop girl and a runaway prince spend one day on the bridge of Via Reye.

stories.title: La Dolce Ponte
stories.logline: One night at the flagship, three proposals and a missing gown.
stories.story: One night at the flagship, three proposals and a missing gown.

stories.title: The Last Ride Out
stories.logline: Two riders share one towel and the last lift before the lanes close for a century.
stories.story: Two riders share one towel and the last lift before the lanes close for a century.

stories.title: Towels at Dawn
stories.logline: A diner, a broken beacon and six riders who all need the same lift.
stories.story: A diner, a broken beacon and six riders who all need the same lift.

stories.title: Pups of the Ring
stories.logline: A runt pup races the whole pack around the moon to win a seat in the arena.
stories.story: A runt pup races the whole pack around the moon to win a seat in the arena.

stories.title: Howl Night
stories.logline: One arena, one microphone, every pup on the moon.

stories.title: Escape Velocity
stories.logline: A pod crew trains one season to win the Belt League in zero gravity.
stories.story: A pod crew trains one season to win the Belt League in zero gravity.

stories.logline: Nine athletes, one locker room, the night before the final.

stories.story: Every night at two in the morning Mara Lune calls the Calder switchboard and talks to whoever answers. She tells the night operator about the laundry on Frontier Street where she ironed the costumes before anyone filmed her, the first screen test where she forgot every line and laughed instead, the raft scene that made her famous and the studio that never let her choose her own parts. By day she is the brightest face on the Calder lot; by night she is a woman planning to buy back her own contract. The calls are the series: each episode is one night, one operator and one secret, until the night she does not call at all because she has finally signed her own name.

stories.story: Penny, Dot and Lady Clementine (who is not a lady) borrow a Mayfair flat from a cousin on a long cruise and pawn the furniture to buy the right hats. The plan is simple: three heiresses, three millionaires, three weddings before the cousin comes home. The millionaires turn out to be a gas-meter baron who talks only about gas, a duke who is mostly debts, and a shy man in tweed who may or may not own Scotland. Meanwhile the doorman, the bus conductor and the fishmonger keep getting in the way. By the final reel the furniture is back, the cruise is early, and all three have married for love, which is the one thing none of them budgeted for.

stories.logline: Princess Amara of Naim falls in love with the white deer of the Saffron Forest, the whole kingdom is stunned, and she still means to win the Naimian Horse Show.
stories.story: Princess Amara of Naim rides out every dawn before the court wakes. One misty morning in the Saffron Forest a white deer with silver antlers steps out of the trees and does not run. She comes back the next day, and the next, and by midsummer she has fallen in love with him. When she walks the deer up to the palace gates the whole of Naim City is stunned: the king drops his teacup, the court tailor faints into a bolt of saffron silk and the royal horses refuse their oats. Amara does not mind. She still loves her horses, still trains Ember every morning for the Naimian Horse Show, and still means to beat the real competitors who come from every world each summer: Callum Reeve on Thunder Vale, Inès Moreau on Saffron Rain, Kaito Hale on Silver Lantern, Freya Lindqvist on North Star and Omar Haddad on Desert Psalm. The deer watches every round from the edge of the arena, and when Ember clears the last fence the kingdom finally understands why she is the best princess Naim has ever had.

The bride is never free; the groom, a quiet prince who knows nothing about silk, keeps turning up to hold the pattern. By the third fitting they are arguing about sleeves, by the fifth they are laughing, and by the last the whole palace is wondering who the gown is really for. The wedding happens, the veil is perfect, and Naim gets the love story nobody planned.

stories.title: One Day in Lora Land
stories.logline: A single June day in the life of a window dresser walking Lora Land from breakfast to two in the morning, every hour told in a different voice.
stories.story: On one Thursday in June, Theo Blum, who dresses the windows of Lora's Spark, goes out at eight to buy his breakfast and does not get home until two in the morning. He buys a cake of lemon soap, goes to a friend's funeral on Ribbon Row, argues about an advertisement at the newspaper office, feeds the gulls on the canal, watches a girl on the Summer Show Lawn at sunset, sits through a rowdy dinner where the young men talk about everything, and follows the poet Kit Dedham into the night district to see him home safe. Every hour of the day is told in a different voice: headlines, a song, a catechism of questions and answers, a play, a list. Theo and Kit share a cup of cocoa in the kitchen and part under the stars. Upstairs, Marion lies awake and remembers the afternoon on the hill when he asked her to marry him, and the story ends with her answer.

stories.logline: A boy learns that the old storyteller who taught him every word has fallen silent for good, and listens to the grown-ups whisper.
stories.story: Every night that summer the boy walks past the shuttered house by Echo Falls and looks for the two candles in the window. When they are lit, he knows the old storyteller Father Fennick has gone quiet for good. In the parlour the storyteller's two sisters serve sherry and crackers and talk in half sentences about a cracked cup and a confession box, and the grown-ups glance at the boy as if he should understand. He does not cry. Walking home along the water he feels oddly free, as if a heavy book had been closed, and tries to remember the last word the old man taught him.

stories.title: The Bazaar at Bozo City
stories.logline: A boy promises to bring his friend's sister a present from the night bazaar, and gets there just as the lights go out.
stories.story: North Row is a quiet street at the far end of Bozo City, and the boy who lives at number seven is in love with Nell Mangan, his friend's older sister. One evening she asks if he is going to the Bazaar, the great night fair in the big top, and he promises to bring her something. On Saturday his uncle comes home late and slow; the boy takes the last tram, which crawls, and reaches the tent as the stalls are closing. Most of the hall is dark. A young woman at a stall of vases and tea sets talks to two men and barely looks at him. He buys nothing. As the lights go out across the big top, he sees himself as a creature driven and mocked by his own wishes, and his eyes burn.

stories.title: Eveline at Dock Nine
stories.logline: A young woman who keeps house for her father has one evening to decide whether to sail away with the man who loves her.
stories.story: Eveline sits at the window of the house on Spray Street and watches the evening come down the canal. Since her mother died she has kept house for her father and the younger children and handed over her wages every Saturday. Frank, a kind sailor, has promised her a home on the far shore, and his ship leaves Dock Nine tonight. She remembers her mother's last words and the promise she made to keep the home together. At the dock, in the crowd and the steam, the ship's horn sounds. Frank takes her hand and goes up the gangway. Eveline grips the iron rail with both hands and cannot move. He calls her name. She looks at him without love or farewell, like a stranger.

stories.story: Maria works in the laundry on Pine Lantern Lane, and on Halloween she has the evening off. She counts her money, buys plum cakes at the bakery and crosses Loon City on the tram to the house of Joe Donnelly, the boy she nursed when he was small. On the tram a kind gentleman talks with her, and she leaves the cakes behind. At the party the children play the old blindfold game: one saucer holds a ring, one a prayer book, one water. Maria's hand touches something soft and wet, there is a silence, and someone quickly takes it away. Later she sings the old song about marble halls, sings the first verse twice by mistake, and nobody tells her. Joe's eyes fill with tears.

stories.title: A Portrait of the Wand-Maker as a Young Man
stories.logline: A boy grows up under the strict masters of the Star Tower and chooses to make things instead of obeying them.
stories.story: Stephen Vane is a small, short-sighted boy at the Star Tower school, where the dormitories are cold and the masters are strict. When a prefect punishes him for broken spectacles that were not his fault, he walks the long corridor to the rector and is believed. As he grows he falls into bad company, hears a sermon so frightening that he runs to confession, and for a while tries to live like a saint; the masters ask him to join their order, and he says no. Walking on the strand he sees a girl standing in the water and understands that his life is to make things, wands and words, not to serve. He argues with his friends about beauty, quarrels with his mother over the old faith and leaves Wand City to make, as he puts it, what his people have never had, calling on the old inventor of wings to stand by him.
stories.after: James Joyce, A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (1916)

stories.title: A Little Cloud
stories.logline: A shy clerk meets his famous old friend for a drink and comes home to find his own life too small.
stories.story: Tommy Chandler spends the afternoon at his desk on Spell Square thinking about Ignatius Gale, his old friend who left Wand City and became a famous writer across the sea. That evening they meet at a bar under the Star Tower. Gale talks about the cities he has seen and orders more drinks; Tommy talks about his wife and baby and feels small and grey. At home his wife goes out to the shops and leaves him with the baby. He tries to read a book of poems he loves, the baby starts to cry and will not stop, and he shouts at it. His wife runs in and comforts the child. Tommy stands back, tears of remorse in his eyes.
stories.after: James Joyce, Dubliners (1914): A Little Cloud

stories.title: The Dead of Once City
stories.logline: At the Marchbank sisters' winter dance a man prepares his speech, and on the way home his wife tells him about a boy who sang to her long ago.
stories.story: Every winter the Marchbank sisters, who keep the oldest watch shop on Carat Court, give a dance for their friends and pupils, and every year their nephew Gideon Conroy carves the goose and makes the speech. This year he worries about his speech, about a quarrel with a guest who calls him a traitor to the old ways, about his galoshes. As the party breaks up a tenor sings an old ballad upstairs, and Greer stops on the dark stairs to listen. At the hotel, when Gideon takes her hand, she cries and tells him about a boy called Michael who used to sing that song, who stood in the rain under her window when he was ill, and who died. She falls asleep. Gideon lies awake and watches the snow falling over all of Once City, on the jewellers' roofs and the quiet churchyard, upon all the living and the dead.
